steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
If you look after a club's admin, keeping the member list tidy is a big job. Today you'll tidy the Earlln Hiking Club member list with Claude.

  1. Find what to tidy, like duplicates and phone formats
  2. Keep the original and make a clean copy
  3. Pull out lists like unpaid dues and birthdays
  4. Draft personalized messages
Personal data caution — everyone in the sample list is fictional. When you show Claude a real list, its contents are sent to Anthropic's servers to produce answers. Check your club's or company's rules first, and mask parts of names or numbers if needed.
  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: a computer where you've done Work 1

steps.title: Get the sample list into Practice
steps.html:
A 15-row member list with name, phone, birthday, join date, November dues and email. (Phone numbers use the fictional 555- prefix.)

⬇ Download the sample members.csv

Drag members.csv from Downloads into the Practice folder.

check.q: Is members.csv in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If getting the file doesn't work
steps.html:
• If clicking shows text on screen, save it with Ctrl+S (⌘+S on a Mac) as members.csv.
  • Moving works like in Work 1.

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: First ask what's in the list
steps.html: With a new file, start by asking what's in it. It's only reading, so no permission needed.
steps.code: Explain what information members.csv has. How many members are there?

check.q: Did it explain the columns and how many members there are?

steps.title: If it can't find the file
steps.html: Check members.csv is inside the Practice folder and the folder under the typing box is Practice.

steps.title: Have it find what to tidy first
steps.html: As in Work 1, have it find problems before fixing. There are 15 rows but only 14 members. Why?
steps.alt: Claude finds a duplicate member, mixed phone formats and blank dues
steps.code: Find what needs tidying in members.csv. Don't fix it yet

check.q: Did it find the duplicate member, the phone formats and the blank dues?

steps.title: If it missed some
steps.html: Three things are hidden: Daniel Lee twice (only the phone format differs), four phone formats (dashes, no spaces, spaces, dots), and blank November dues for 2 people. Giving criteria helps, e.g. "Also find people with the same name and birthday."

steps.title: Keep the original; make a clean copy
steps.html: State the rules clearly. In particular, don't let it turn blank dues into 'Unpaid' on its own. Read the create-file card and click Allow.
steps.code: Leave the original as is and make a new members_clean.csv. Keep only one row for the duplicate, use the 555-0000 format for all phone numbers, and write 'Check' where dues are blank. Save it so Excel opens it correctly

steps.title: If the clean copy looks off
steps.html:
• 15 members means the duplicate is still there: "Daniel Lee appears twice. Keep only one row."
  • If a card edits the original, deny it and say "Don't touch the original; make a new file."

steps.title: Pull out the lists you need
steps.html: Let's pull the two lists club admins look for most.
steps.alt: Lists of unpaid or unchecked dues and December birthdays
steps.code: From members_clean.csv, list who hasn't paid or needs checking for November dues, and December birthdays

check.q: Did you get 3 unpaid (Jamie Park, Sue Cho, Chloe Lim), 2 to check (Hannah Jung, Yuna Oh) and 5 December birthdays?

steps.title: If the lists differ
steps.html:
• If Daniel Lee appears twice among birthdays, the duplicate is still there.
  • If the 2 blanks were counted as unpaid: "Blank isn't unpaid; list those separately as 'Check'."

steps.title: Draft personalized messages
steps.html:
Ask for a message with each person's name, all at once. Have it leave things it can't know, like account numbers, as blanks instead of making them up.

Claude Code doesn't send messages. Check the drafts, then copy and send them yourself.
steps.code: Write a polite reminder message for each of the 3 unpaid members, with their names. Leave the account number as [ACCOUNT]

check.q: Did you get 3 messages with names, and [ACCOUNT] left blank?

steps.title: If it invented an account number
steps.html: Never use a made-up number. Say "Don't invent the account number; leave it as [ACCOUNT]." Also check names and amounts against the list.

steps.title: Try handing over these too
steps.html:
• Add a new member: "Add new member Sky Kim, 555-1315, 1992-05-05, joined today, dues Paid, to members_clean.csv"
  • Birthday messages: "A short birthday message for members born in December"
  • Attendance sheet: "Make a December hike attendance sheet from members_clean.csv"
  • Members who've drifted away: if you keep attendance, "members absent for over 3 months"
After working with a real list, delete leftover copies in the Practice folder and keep the clean copy somewhere safe.

steps.title: 🎉 Work practice 5 done! What you learned
steps.html:
You untangled a list, pulled out the lists you needed and drafted messages.

Three things to remember

  1. Personal data: a real list's contents are sent to the server when Claude reads it. Check the rules and mask if needed.
  2. State the rules clearly: "phone numbers in this format", "blank means Check", so it doesn't change things on its own.
  3. No inventions: leave unknowns like account numbers blank. Check names and amounts before sending.
